subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & data isolation needs (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & data isolation needs (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned on next steps and the specific data isolation questions you raised: 

Key customer priorities you shared:
- Absolute data isolation for PII and financial records.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) either in-cloud or on-prem.
- Audit logs and retention policies that meet your internal compliance (7 years preferred).
- Network-level isolation (no public internet egress for inference calls).
- Clarification on whether any customer data is ever used for model training or shared with other tenants.

Where we think each deployment mode fits based on the call:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started but runs on multi-tenant Redwood infrastructure — encrypted in transit/at-rest, but not ideal for strict data isolation needs.
- Dedicated: dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation at the runtime level; good for predictable throughput and stronger logical isolation. Typically suitable when the customer is ok with Redwood-managed infra + strict tenancy and encryption controls.
- Private VPC / On-prem: provides private control plane, VPC peering or on-prem install; allows customer-managed keys, private networking, and full audit/OBL options — the best fit for regulated financials.

Questions I have for you (so we can scope the right engagement):
1) Is FinSecure open to Redwood-managed infrastructure if we provide customer-managed keys + strict tenant isolation (Dedicated), or do you require a Private VPC / on-prem deployment?
2) Any specific networking constraints (e.g., must not cross to public subnets, require no egress to AWS-managed services, set of allowed IPs)?
3) Who will be the procurement/compliance contact to review SOC 2 and pen test reports?

Attachments: I have SOC2 and a network diagram I can share. Also attaching a short questionnaire that helps us finalize if Dedicated will suffice or if we should propose Private VPC.

Next step: propose a 30–45 minute security deep-dive with Rishi (SE) and Vivek (AE) this week — does Thursday 7/16 11am PT work for you?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and follow-ups from our side: 
- Prefer Private VPC if it eliminates any chance of cross-tenant data exposure. If Dedicated provides strong tenant isolation and supports CMK, we could evaluate it, but preference is Private.
- Networking: we require no public egress for inference traffic; outgoing calls must be restricted to our internal IP ranges.
- Procurement/compliance contact: Bob Lee (cc'd) will own SOC2 review and procurement.

A few technical clarifications for the security call: 
1) In Dedicated mode, is the KV/prefix cache strictly per-tenant and automatically purged between sessions?
2) Does Redwood ever write customer request/response data to long-term storage that could be used for training or model improvements?
3) How do you handle CMKs in Dedicated vs Private VPC (who holds master keys)?

Thursday 7/16 11am PT works for us. Looking forward to the security deep-dive.

Thanks,
Alice
Director of Engineering, FinSecure
alice.johnson@finsecure.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@finsecure.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@finsecure.com>

Subject: RE: Follow-up: deployment mode & data isolation needs (Dedicated vs Private VPC) — answers ahead of call

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks — I wanted to get a short set of answers in advance of our call so we can focus on specifics: 

1) KV / prefix cache behavior (Dedicated):
- Cache is logically scoped per-tenant and we do not share prefixes across tenants. For Dedicated capacity, each customer's inference requests use isolated runtime containers and per-tenant KV namespaces.
- Cache lifecycle: entries are ephemeral by default (session-scoped), and we can configure automatic purge policies (e.g., purge after X hours) for regulated workloads. We can also disable prefix caching if required.

2) Long-term storage and training: 
- Redwood does not use customer request/response logs to train public models. We treat customer data as non-training data by default; any use for model improvements would only occur with an explicit customer opt-in and contract.
- For Hosted and Dedicated we store short-term logs for debugging/observability — retention is configurable and we can turn off long-term retention or route logs to customer-managed storage in Private deployments.

3) Customer-managed keys (CMK) & KMS/HSM: 
- Dedicated: we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed master keys by default; we can support customer-supplied CMKs in supported cloud providers for Dedicated tenants (subject to contract).
- Private VPC / On-prem: full support for customer-managed keys and HSM integrations (bring-your-own-key) — keys never leave your key boundary in these setups.

Additional notes: 
- Network isolation: Private VPC supports VPC peering or private endpoints and can be configured to prevent public internet egress. On-prem provides full air-gapped options.
- Audit logs & retention: Private VPC gives you access to the control plane audit logs and the option to ship them directly to your logging/siem. Dedicated can provide aggregated audit artifacts and per-request traces on request.

Attachments I've uploaded to the shared drive ahead of the call: SOC2_report_v2.pdf (redacted), redwood_network_diagram.png, data_isolation_qs.xlsx.

If you'd like, we can prepare an implementation checklist (network rules, CIDR ranges, KMS setup steps) to speed procurement.

See you at 11.
Rishi
